claims.text: Greg LaVecchia asserts that taking full responsibility for everything in one's environment is the primary driver of personal development: the sooner a person does this, the better they become. The mechanism is that accepting ownership of circumstances — rather than attributing them to external forces — is what drives growth.
claims.speaker: Greg LaVecchia
claims.mechanism: Accepting ownership of circumstances rather than attributing outcomes to external forces removes the psychological exit that blocks growth; without the escape valve of blame, the individual is forced to develop.

claims.text: Greg LaVecchia argues that entering one's 20s having already developed independence and personal accountability confers a meaningful competitive advantage over peers who enter the same phase still lacking those traits. He frames this as entering the arena ahead of the competition.
claims.speaker: Greg LaVecchia
conditions: individual develops independence and accountability in late teens (before entering 20s)
context is competitive environments — careers, entrepreneurship, or any arena requiring self-direction
bounded_by: LaVecchia does not specify whether the advantage is permanent or only an early lead that can be closed later

practices.text: Develop independence and personal accountability in your late teens, before entering your 20s, so that you carry those traits into competitive arenas from the start.
